title: Turkey Stuffed Green Peppers
description: Try this kidney-friendly recipe for Turkey Stuffed Green Peppers at your next dinner.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Remove stems from peppers and clean seeds and membranes from inside.
Mix turkey, rice, egg, onion, garlic and seasonings well.
Stuff peppers with meat mixture.
Place peppers in a large roaster.
Pour crushed tomatoes and broth over peppers
Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes.
hints: Use ground turkey breast for the leanest possible filling, but lean ground beef and lean ground pork tenderloin are also heart-healthy fillings.
If you are not on a potassium restricted diet, use a 16-oz. can of crushed tomatoes.
Make a double batch and freeze individual peppers for an easy meal when you don’t feel like cooking.

Stuffed peppers are ubiquitous throughout Central and Eastern Europe. Seasoning and what type of meat with which they are stuffed vary not only from region to region, but within regions. Some use 100% ground beef, others use 100% ground pork, and others use a mixture.
For a lower protein diet you can use one pound of turkey and increase the rice to 3 cups.

title: Watermelon Agua Fresca
description: Fresh water blended with watermelon and lime juice is a perfect thirst quencher for a hot summer day or anytime. Watermelon Agua Fresca is low in potassium making it a great choice for a kidney diet.
steps: Cut the lime into slices. Cut the watermelon into large chunks and measure 2 cups.
Place the watermelon in a blender along with 2 lime slices and blend until smooth.
Use a sieve to strain the mixture and pour into 4 cups. Garnish with mint leaves and lime slices and serve.
hints: Replace sugar with stevia sweetener to reduce carbohydrates to 12 grams.

title: Pineapple Non-Dairy “Ice Cream” Treats
description: Only four ingredients and no cooking required makes Pineapple Non-Dairy "ice Cream" treats budget-friendly and easy to make.
ingredients: 20 ounce can crushed pineapple, well drained
steps: Mix drained pineapple and protein powder well, fold in the whipped topping.
Place a single layer of graham cracker squares on a cookie sheet and spread about 2 tablespoons topping mixture on each cracker.
Place another graham cracker square on top and place cookie sheet in the freezer.
When well frozen, wrap individually in plastic wrap and store them in an airtight container in the freezer.
hints: Some whipped toppings have phosphorus additives. Look at the ingredients list to be sure phosphorus is not added.
A 14.4 ounce box of graham crackers contains about 27 rectangle sheets.
Protein powder can vary in protein, potassium, phosphorus and sodium. You may talk to your dietitian to see which one would be appropriate for you.

title: Green Beans a la Roast
description: Never before have you tasted veggies like these! DaVita renal dietitian Brady from Ohio shows us how to roast green beans so they’re tender and tantalizing! With this dish, you won’t have to worry about getting your kids to eat their vegetables. And it also fits into a kidney-friendly diet so you can be sure that everyone will be asking for seconds of Green Beans a la Roast!
steps: Preheat oven to 450° F.
Wash green beans and trim ends.
Line a rimmed baking sheet with aluminum foil and spread beans on foil.
Pour olive oil over beans and toss gently to coat beans evenly.
Roast in oven for 10 minutes.
Remove baking sheet from oven and redistribute beans for even baking.
Return to oven and bake for approximately 10 additional minutes or until beans have a few golden brown areas.
Remove from oven, season with ground pepper and serve.
hints: For extra flavor try a flavored oil with llemon or herb flavor.

title: Coconut Bread
description: Shredded coconut and sour cream give kidney-friendly Coconut Bread the perfect balance of sweetness and moistness. Add some pineapple to turn it into a Hawaiian treat.
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Grease a 9 x 5-inch loaf pan. Set butter out to soften.
Warm coconut oil in microwave until just melted. Set aside to cool.
Cream butter and sugar together. Add coconut oil and eggs; stir together. Mix in sour cream. Add shredded coconut to mixture and stir.
In a separate bowl mix together flour, baking soda and baking powder.
Fold dry ingredients into wet ingredients. Pour batter into the loaf pan.
Bake 45 to 60 minutes, until bread is golden brown and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool bread in pan for 5 to 10 minutes then remove from pan and cool on a wire rack.
hints: If desired add 1/2 cup of diced or crushed pineapple.
Wrap some of the bread slices in freezer wrap and freeze for a quick snack later.

title: Poached Pears
description: Ready to transformplain pears into a tasty dessert? DaVita renal dietitian, Geri from Washington will show you how to make delicious foods for the kidney diet with her kidney-friendly recipe for Poached Pears.
steps: Mix cinnamon and sugar in a small bowl.
Cut pears in half and using a spoon scoop out seeds and stem.
Make a thin slice across round part of pear, so that it lays flat in baking dish.
Place pears skin side down in a baking dish and sprinkle tops with cinnamon and sugar mix.
Place 1 teaspoon butter in the seed hole of each pear.
Pour juice in bottom of pan.
Cover with foil and bake at 350° F approximately 30 minutes or until pear is soft when poked with fork.
hints: If your baking dish is shallow you may need less juice. The juice should only come halfway up the side of the pears.
Pour juice over pears before serving if desired.
For people with diabetes use low calorie cranberry juice and subar substitute instead of sugar.

title: Asparagus Cauliflower Tortilla
description: Cindy, a DaVita renal dietitian from Wisconsin, focuses on her patient’s individual kidney dietary wishes and tries to make them a reality. A delicious, dialysis diet recipe such as her tasty and filling Asparagus Cauliflower Tortilla is simple to prepare and will satisfy your hunger, keep your taste buds happy and help make your dreams of healthy lab results come true.
ingredients: 2 cups asparagus, chopped in bite size pieces
2 cups cauliflower, chopped in bite size pieces
1 cup liquid low cholesterol egg substitute
steps: Place asparagus and cauliflower pieces plus 1 tablespoon water in a microwave-proof, covered dish. Microwave for 3 to 5 minutes to steam until tender crisp.
Sauté the onion until golden, about 7 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook, stirring, 1 minute longer.
Stir in the asparagus, cauliflower, egg substitute, parsley, salt, pepper, thyme and nutmeg.
Reduce heat and cook covered until set and browned on bottom, about 10 to 15 minutes.
Loosen the edges with a knife and invert onto a warm platter or serve directly from skillet.
hints: In Spain and South America, a tortilla is a round, unfolded omelet typically made with eggs, vegetables and seasonings. In comparison, the Mexican tortilla is thin, flat bread made from wheat flour or ground corn.

title: Roasted Cauliflower with Rosemary
description: Cauliflower could easily become your favorite low potassium vegetable after tasting Roasted Cauliflower with Rosemary. Created by the DaVita dietitian team, this veggie roast is lightly seasoned with oil, a small amount of salt, pepper and fresh rosemary. Roasted Cauliflower with Rosemary is easy to make and kidney-friendly.
steps: Preheat oven to 450° F.
Cut cauliflower florets into bite-size pieces. Chop rosemary.
In a large bowl, toss cauliflower with remaining ingredients.
Spread seasoned cauliflower on an ungreased baking sheet.
Roast for 15 minutes; remove from oven and stir.
Continue roasting for 10 minutes or until cauliflower is tender and lightly browned.
hints: Use caution when removing baking sheet from oven to stir cauliflower.

title: Italian Style Vegetables & Pasta with Chicken
description: Try the kidney-friendly recipe for Italian Style Vegetables & Pasta with Chicken for your next big dinner.
steps: Chop bell pepper and onion. Dice chicken.
Place oil in a large nonstick frying pan and stir-fry the bell pepper, onion and broccoli. Sprinkle with the rosemary, basil, red pepper flakes, garlic powder and salt.
Stir in the cooked chicken.
Mix chicken broth with cornstarch and add to vegetable and chicken mixture. Cook until thickened slightly. Stir in the cup of hot cooked pasta.
Remove from heat and serve.
hints: Chicken may be increased to 6 ounces for those on dialysis. Protein content will be increased to 29 grams per serving.
For quick preparation, use 1-1/4 cups of a frozen vegetable mixture of similar composition to replace fresh vegetables.
Add more or less red pepper flakes to suit your own tolerance for spicy foods.
Squeeze on lemon juice or sprinkle with balsamic vinegar to add a tangy flavor.

title: Ground Beef and Veggie Foil Pack Dinner
description: Easy to assemble and easy to clean up is a perfect description for DaVita dietitian Graces’ recipe, Ground Beef and Veggie Foil Pack Dinner. Plus you can vary the type of protein and veggies to make this recipe an easy go-to kidney-friendly dinner.
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F. Spray a piece of foil with nonstick cooking spray. Chop the onion.
Combine the ground beef, onion and Worcestershire sauce into a patty and place on the foil.
Top patty with frozen peas and carrots.
Sprinkle Italian dressing mix and black pepper over the top.
Fold and seal the foil and place on a baking sheet. Bake for 35 minutes.
Carefully open one end of the foil packet and allow steam to escape before serving.
hints: Spray the foil with cooking spray.
Place the foil packet on a baking sheet before placing in the oven.

title: Hazelnut Cinnamon Coffee
description: Start the day off on a delicious note with the kidney-friendly recipe for Hazelnut Cinnamon Coffee.
ingredients: 8 teaspoons Torani® Sugar Free Classic Hazelnut Syrup
steps: Brew coffee in coffee maker. Pour into small cups.
Add 2 teaspoons of the Torani® Sugar Free Classic Hazelnut Syrup and 1 tablespoon of milk (or creamer) to each mug and garnish each with a cinnamon stick.
hints: Try different flavors of the Torani® Sugar Free syrups.
If you prefer your coffee darker, omit the milk.
Many nondairy creamers contain phosphate additives. Be aware if you substitute nondairy hazelnut creamer for the syrup.

title: Cinnamon Roll Cake
description: Ingredients Preparation Helpful hints
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Melt 1/2 cup butter and leave remaining butter out to soften.
In medium-sized bowl, mix 3 cups flour, salt, 1 cup Splenda baking blend, baking soda, cream of tartar, 1-1/2 cups Rice Dream, eggs and 2 teaspoons vanilla. Slowly stir in melted butter.
Pour mixture into a greased 9″ x 13″ pan.
Mix 1 cup softened butter, Splenda brown sugar blend, 2 tablespoons flour and cinnamon until well combined. Drop evenly over the batter and swirl with a knife.
Bake for 28-32 minutes.
Combine remaining 1 cup Splenda baking blend and powdered sugar, 5 tablespoons rice milk and 1 teaspoon vanilla. Drizzle over cake while it’s still warm.
hints: This high calorie dessert is great for boosting calories. Enjoy for breakfast or dessert.
If available,1 cup Ideal® powdered sugar substitute may be used to replace 1 cup Splenda baking blend and 1 cup powdered sugar to reduce calories and carbohydrates.

title: Turkey Meatloaf
description: Sara’s kidney-friendly recipe for Turkey Meatloaf features a bit of hot turkey sausage, providing a kick you don’t expect but will really enjoy.Turkey Meatloaf may look familiar, but will introduce you to a whole new flavor.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Gravy Master® seasoning & browning sauce
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl and mix well.
Transfer to a greased 9″ x 5″ loaf pan and bake for 1 hour.
Slice into 6 equal pieces and serve.
hints: Select the brand of sausage lowest in sodium.
Use the hot and spicy turkey sausage for more flavor.

title: Pomegranate Refresher
description: Pomegranate juice, lemon juice and club soda are combined to create this festive, sparkling Pomegranate Refresher.
steps: Add pomegranate and lemon juice to a small glass.
Top with club soda.
Add in pomegranate arils and garnish with lemon.
hints: Pomegranate juice is limited to 1/4 cup in this recipe. One cup of pomegranate juice contains over 500 mg potassium.
Substitute cranberry juice for pomegranate juice if preferred. Potassium is decreased to 46 mg.
Add a small amount of your favorite sweetener for added sweetness.

title: Lamb or Mutton Stew with Dumplings
description: If you’ve never tried it, or don’t serve it often, DaVita renal dietitian, Miriam from Arizona, has a Lamb or Mutton Stew with Dumplings recipe that is tasty, renal-friendly and a one-dish meal that cooks everything in a single pot.
steps: Measure water and put in a stew pot.
Trim fat from meat and cut into bite-size pieces. Add meat and bones to water. Set on stove over medium heat.
Coarsely chop onion. Cut zucchini in half lengthwise and sliced into 1/2” slices
Add onion, zucchini and chilies to stew.
Once the stew has come to a low boil, turn heat to low and let simmer for at least 1 hour.
While stew is cooking, mix flour, salt, baking powder and sugar in a bowl.
Knead in warm water to dry ingredients to form a soft ball of dough.
Cover dough and let it rest for 20 to 30 minutes.
After cooking stew for 1 hour, shape an approximately 2-1/2” dough ball into a flat round. (It does not need to be perfect or flat).
Tear off penny-sized pieces of dough and drop them into the stew.
Continue to shape 2-1/2” dough ball into a flat round and tear off penny-sized pieces of dough and drop in stew until all dough is in stew.
Cook dumplings in the stew for an additional 20 minutes.
Serve and enjoy.
hints: Roast 2-3 Hatch chilies instead of canned chilies.

title: Shake and Bake Chicken Extravaganza
description: Patience isn’t just a virtue, it’s a talent. Just like cooking, developing compassion is a skill that can be perfected, as Mary, a DaVita renal dietitian from Minnesota has demonstrated. Mary has honed her skill for “patience with patients,” as well as, her inventiveness for creating delicious recipes, such as her kidney-friendly Shake and Bake Chicken Extravaganza.
serving_size: 1 piece of chicken (3 ounces without bone)
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F.
Grease baking sheet with vegetable oil (can use parchment paper or silpat sheet) and set aside.
Combine bread crumbs, flour, parsley, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, black pepper, marjoram and thyme. Stir to mix evenly.
Add oil to bread crumb mixture and stir with a fork to blend completely.
Store in airtight container in cool, dry place or store in freezer.
To prepare chicken: Rinse chicken with water and leave chicken pieces moist with water while shaking off excess liquid.
Pour 1 cup of bread crumb mixture into a clean plastic food storage bag. Add 1 to 2 pieces of chicken at a time to bag and shake to coat evenly.
Place on greased baking sheet and bake for 40 to 45 minutes. Turn once, after 20 minutes.
hints: This recipe makes enough coating mix for 3 meals. Store the remaining mixture in a sealed container or freezer bag and freeze until ready to use again.
To homemade dry breadcrumbs, toast day old bread until crisp but not burned. Crush in a blender or food processor.

title: Roasted Brussels Sprouts, Carrots and Apples
description: Enhance the flavor of fall vegetables by roasting and adding a hint of maple syrup. Roasted Brussels Sprouts, Carrots and Apples is a kidney-friendly recipe, easy for any dinner and special enough to serve at special dinners.
steps: Preheat the oven to 375° F. Spray a baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray.
Trim the Brussels sprouts and cut each one in half. Peel the carrots and cut into 1-inch pieces. Core the apple and cut into 1/2-inch cubes.
Place Brussels sprouts, carrots and apple pieces in a large bowl.
In a small bowl combine the olive oil, maple syrup and spices. Stir to combine.
Pour sauce into the large bowl and stir to coat vegetables and apples. Place ingredients on the baking sheet. Sprinkle with the 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes until carrots are fork tender and Brussels sprouts begin to darken.
hints: Replace carrots with 2 medium turnips if desired.
Add leftovers to mixed salad greens for a hearty roasted veggie salad the next day.

title: Shrimp Boulettes
description: Shrimp Boulettes are a seafood lovers delight because crab or crawfish can easily be substituted for shrimp. Created by DaVita patient Ken in Louisiana, Shrimp Boulettes give a kidney-friendly twist to an old-time Cajun favorite.
ingredients: 1/2 cup to 1 cup all-purpose white flour
steps: Finely chop shrimp, onion, bell pepper and parsley. Beat eggs.
Mix all of the ingredients except flour together in a mixing bowl.
After mixing, gradually add flour. Continue adding flour a little at a time until mix gets thick and hangs on to the spoon.
To deep fry, heat oil in a large skillet or deep-fryer. Drop medium-sized spoonfuls of shrimp batter into hot oil and cook until browned and crisp on both sides.
Remove from oil and drain on paper towels. Serve hot.
hints: Suggested Cajun seasonings include homemade Salt-free Cajun Seasoning on DaVita.com, Mrs. Dash Cajun seasoning blend or Benoit’s Best Salt-Free Cajun seasoning. Avoid products with potassium chloride.
Instead of frying you can form batter into patties and bake on a greased baking sheet at 350° F until golden brown.
Try crab or crawfish instead of shrimp. Both are equally great!

title: Berries Napoleon
description: Indulge your sweet tooth on the renal diet with Berries Napoleon, a simple, delicious dessert from renal dietitian Marie from Colorado. On its own or paired with an elegant meal, this low potassium dessert is perfect for the kidney diet.
steps: Preheat oven to 400° F.
Spray the cooking spray on a baking sheet that will fit 12 wonton wrappers.
Spread out the wonton wrappers, and spray them with cooking spray.
Sprinkle the granulated sugar on wonton wrappers.
Bake the wontons for 5 minutes or until golden brown;remove from the baking sheet.
Place 6 wonton wrappers on a serving tray.
Top each wrapper with 2 tablespoons of whipped topping, 1 tablespoon of raspberries and 1 tablespoon of blueberries.
Top the berries with a second wonton wrapper.
Sprinkle the tops with powdered sugar. Garnish them with a dollop of whipped topping, fruit and a mint leaf, if desired. Serve immediately.
hints: Substitute strawberries and blackberries for raspberries and blueberries for variety.
To reduce carbohydrate content substitute Splenda® No Calorie granular sweetener for sugar.
If the wontons sit in the refrigerator the Reddi-Wip will melt. Assemble only when ready to serve.

title: Poppy Krunch
description: Looking for a quick snack that is light, crunchy and sweet? DaVita renal dietitian Jackie from North Carolina has the answer: Poppy Krunch. Kids will love this treat made from popcorn that’s been drizzled with a buttery-sweet topping, but adults will want their fair share too. And since it’s kidney-friendly, those with renal problems are able to indulge without
steps: Spread popcorn in a shallow pan.
Combine sugar, corn syrup and butter in a 1/2-quart saucepan.
Cook over medium heat until a small amount dropped in cold water separates into thin threads which are hard but not brittle (280° F on the candy thermometer). Remove from heat.
Add vanilla.
Pour syrup over popcorn, stirring until well-coated. Spread on a greased baking sheet. Break into pieces.
Allow to cool. Store in an air tight container until ready to serve.
hints: Portion into individual servings and store for a quick snack or dessert during the week.

title: Easy Turkey Sloppy Joes
description: Enjoy a savory, family favorite that celebrates the Americana diner of yesteryear. DaVita renal dietitian, Tammy from Louisiana, shares a kidney-friendly recipe for Easy Turkey Sloppy Joes.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Mrs. Dash® Chicken Grilling Blend seasoning
steps: Chop onion and bell pepper.
Place in a large skillet with turkey and cook over medium high heat until turkey is cooked through. Do not drain.
In a small bowl, mix together the Mrs. Dash® seasoning, sugar, Worcestershire sauce and tomato sauce.
Add seasonings to the turkey mixture. Reduce heat to simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
Divide into 6 portions and serve on hamburger buns.
hints: Lean ground beef may be substituted for ground turkey. Drain the fat after browning the beef in preparation step one.
To save time, use frozen chopped onions and bell pepper.
For a lower-protein diet, reduce turkey to 1 pound or portion can be adjusted according to your diet plan.

title: Slow Cooker Honey Baked Apples
description: For your next dessert craving, try the kidney-friendly recipe for Slow Cooker Honey Baked Apples. Our recipe for Slow Cooker Honey Baked Apples was created exclusively for DaVita.com by DaVita renal dietitian Sara from California. This modern, kidney-friendly take on classic baked apples is perfect for those following diabetes, dialysis and CKD non-dialysis diets.
steps: Core and cut each apple into 8 pieces and place in a slow cooker.
Sprinkle cinnamon over apple pieces and toss to coat.
Drizzle with honey, add butter and stir.
Set slow cooker to low temperature, cover with a lid and cook for 2 hours.
hints: This recipe can also be prepared in the oven. Cook at 325° F for 45 to 60 minutes.

title: German Apple Cake
description: German Apple Cake is a combination of sweet apples sliced and stirred into a sweet lemony-cinnamon batter which is then baked until golden brown. This kidney-friendly cake is so tasty that no icing is needed.
steps: Preheat the oven to 325° F. Grease a 9 x 13-inch baking dish. Set butter out to soften. Peel, core and slice apples.

Using a mixer, cream the butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Zest the lemon. Add the lemon zest and vanilla extract to butter and sugar mixture. Add one egg and continue to mix; add the other egg and mix.
In a separate bowl combine the flour, cinnamon, baking soda and salt. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the creamed butter until combined. Do not over mix.
Juice the lemon; stir the juice into the batter. Stir in the apple slices.

Pour the batter into the greased baking dish. Sprinkle one tablespoon of sugar over the top. Bake for 30 to 40 minutes. The cake is done when a toothpick inserted into the middle of the cake comes out clean. After cake is cool cut into 15 pieces and serve.
hints: Use apple variety of choice.
Cut the cake into 20 pieces for a lower carbohydrate serving (23 grams).

title: Super Fruit Smoothie
description: Marlene, a DaVita dietitian from Florida, says she looks after her patients like a “mother hen.” And, like most moms, she likes to provide good-for-you treats. Marlene’s Super Fruit Smoothie is a perfect, kidney-friendly treat.
ingredients: 8 ounces Vanilla Nepro® with Carb Steady™, chilled
1 cup of frozen peaches or mixed berries
steps: Add frozen fruit to blender.
Add chilled Nepro®, whey protein and crushed ice (if desired).
Blend until smooth.
Pour into glass and serve with straw.
hints: Freeze or refrigerate the leftover portion for later.
Recipe analysis used values for Beneprotein® whey protein powder, 7 gram size scoops. Nutrient values may vary slightly with similar products.

title: Angelina’s Gingerbread Muffins
description: Angelina’s Gingerbread Muffins are sure to be a holiday favorite for years to come. Spicy ginger combined with cinnamon and brown sugar come together to create a scrumptious kidney-friendly muffin that’s great for breakfast, dessert or snack.
steps: Preheat oven to 400° F. Grease a 12-cup muffin pan or line with paper liners.
In a medium bowl lightly beat the eggs. Beat in the milk, oil, brown sugar and corn syrup.

In a large bowl stir together the flour, baking powder, ginger, and cinnamon. Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and pour in the liquid ingredients. Stir gently until just combined: do not over mix.
Spoon the batter into the prepared muffin pan. Bake in the preheated oven for about 20 minutes, until golden brown and firm to the touch.
Remove from oven and let the muffins cool in the pan for 5 minutes. Serve warm with butter or cream cheese.
hints: Freeze leftover muffins for a quick snack later. Reheat in microwave for 30-45 seconds.
Muffins contain baking powder that contributes to phosphorus content. Ask your dietitian if you need to take a phosphate binder when muffins are eaten as a snack.

title: Broccoli-Onion Latkes (Pancakes)
description: Renal dietitian Marjorie from Arizona shares the kidney-friendly recipe for Broccoli-Onion Latkes (pancakes) that use onion and broccoli as alternatives to potatoes for low-potassium latkes that can be enjoyed by anyone, even those on renal-friendly diets.
steps: Dice broccoli and chop onion.
Boil the diced broccoli in a small amount of water for 5 minutes; drain.
Break eggs into a medium bowl and beat. Add the flour and mix well.
Add the broccoli and onion and stir into the flour/egg mixture until well mixed.
Add olive oil to a frying pan and heat.
Drop the mixture by spoonfuls into the hot oil, making 4 equal portions (or 8 portions is smaller latkes are desired).
Using a spatula, flatten the latkes and fry until brown on both sides.
Drain on a paper towel to soak up extra oil.
Serve hot.
hints: Potato latkes (pancakes), traditionally served during Hanukkah, contain over 600 mg potassium for a comparable serving unless the potatoes are soaked or boiled to reduce potassium. Broccoli-Onion Latkes are a good low-potassium alternative.
The latkes taste best if eaten immediately.

title: Breakfast Trail Mix
description: DaVita dietitian Wai Yin makes sure her dialysis patients start the day with breakfast. She shares a quick, on the run recipe for Breakfast Trail Mix. With only 4 ingredients it’s easy to make and can be eaten with or without milk or lower potassium and phosphorus milk substitute.
ingredients: 1/2 cup mini rice cakes (plain or apple cinnamon)
steps: In a medium bowl mix all ingredients together.
Divide into 1 cup portions.
Serve dry or with your favorite milk substitute.
hints: Breakfast Trail Mix is a great breakfast alternative for dialysis patients who often do not have time for breakfast. It can be eaten as a snack or with milk alternative as a breakfast cereal.
Be creative and experiment with different cereals. Ask your dietitian for a list of approved cereals.

title: Chickpea Burgers with Tzatziki Sauce
description: Chickpea Burgers with Tzatziki Sauce is the perfect pick to help boost fiber in a plant-based meal.
serving_size: 1 burger in pita, 1/4 cup tzatziki sauce
ingredients: 1/2 recipe Tzatziki Sauce from the DaVita.com recipe
steps: Prepare the Tzatziki Sauce and refrigerate until ready to use.
Rinse and drain the chickpeas. Trim and slice the scallions. Slice the onion.

In a food processor, combine chickpeas, scallions, egg, flour, oregano, cumin and salt. Blend and pulse until a course mixture forms that holds together when pressed. The mixture will be moist. Form into 4 patties.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. When hot, add patties. Cook until golden and beginning to crisp, 4 to 5 minutes. Flip and cook until golden brown and crisp, 2 to 4 minutes more.
Warm the pitas and cut each in half.
Assemble burgers by carefully splitting pita halves open. Cut a chickpea burger in half and place the two halves inside pita as pictured, topping with tzatziki sauce and red onion slice.
hints: Add lettuce and cucumbers for extra crunch.
Chickpeas are also known as garbanzo beans. Compare labels and select the lowest sodium product.

title: Chinese Rice Noodles
description: In Asian culture a dish of unbroken noodles is eaten to bring good luck and health in the New Year. This kidney-friendly Chinese Rice Noodles recipe keeps sodium lower by replacing traditional soy sauce with lower sodium coconut aminos.
ingredients: 4 leaves from large head of bok choy (1 cup chopped)
3/4 cup unsalted beef or vegetable broth
steps: Prepare rice sticks according to package instructions (typically cover sticks with cold water for 20 minutes and then separate).
Slice the bok choy, celery and carrot into thin slices. Dice the onion; mince the garlic.
In a small bowl, combine coconut aminos, broth, chili sauce, garlic and corn starch.
Heat a pan over medium-high heat and add canola and sesame oils. Add the diced onion and cook until translucent. Add the bok choy, celery and carrot slices and stir-fry until tender crisp.
Add sauce to cooked vegetables and stir to combine.
Once the rice sticks have softened, separate the noodles and add to pan with sauce and vegetables. Stir all to combine.
Let sit 15 minutes prior to serving for flavors to fully develop.
Slice green onion and sprinkle on top to garnish before serving.
hints: Rice sticks are also known as rice noodles.
You can substitute soba, udon, vermicelli or spaghetti for rice noodles. Prepare according to instructions instead of soaking.
Add tofu, shrimp or chicken to make a meal.
Coconut aminos replace soy sauce or tamari in this recipe to keep sodium lower.

title: Falafel
description: Falafel, a Middle-Eastern favorite, is versatile for a snack, meal or salad topping. The main ingredient is chickpeas, a fiber-boosting legume that adds to the healthiness. Add garlic sauce and fresh cucumbers for additional flavor.
steps: Cover chickpeas in water in a large pot and soak overnight at room temperature.
Finely chop the white onion; chop green onions, parsley and garlic.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Place in a food processor along with the green onion, white onion, parsley, garlic, lemon juice, flour, salt, coriander, cumin, black pepper and cayenne pepper.

Pulse until mixture reaches a course meal to paste texture. (Do not over process). You may have to do this in 2 batches depending on size of your food processor. Once done, blend together with a fork and remove any large pieces of chickpeas.
Refrigerate the falafel mixture for 2 hours.
Preheat oven to 400° F.
Spray a muffin tin with cooking spray.
Use a scoop or roll mixture into 24 balls; add directly into muffin tin. Place in the oven and bake for 7 minutes. Remove, turn falafel over, and then bake 7 minutes longer.
hints: Serve falafel in a pita pocket with cucumbers, lettuce, onions and garlic sauce or on top of a salad.
If patties are not forming you may need to put back in food processor until they are more paste like. Be careful not to process into hummus like texture.
You can add more flour to help bind.
If desired you can fry falafel in oil instead of baking. Use cooking oil with a high smoke point such as grapeseed or peanut oil.
Substitute falafel for a protein food instead of in addition to help keep phosphorus and potassium intake in goal.

title: Green Pea Salad
description: Sweet green peas, red onion and a small amount of sliced black olives and mozzarella cheese combined in a creamy yogurt mayonnaise sauce make this Green Pea Salad recipe simple but tasty. It’s perfect for lunch, dinner, or to take to a potluck event.
steps: Chop the onion and mince the basil.
In a small bowl combine the mayonnaise and yogurt.
Cook the peas in boiling water for 2 to 3 minutes. Drain and then mix peas with the mayonnaise-yogurt sauce while peas are still warm.
Add the onion, basil and olives to the green pea mixture and stir to combine ingredients.
Sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top and refrigerate until ready to serve.
hints: Three cups of green peas is approximately 1 pound. Substitute fresh green peas when in season.
Choose mayonnaise with an olive oil base to include healthy fats.
Use parsley in place of basil if desired.
Two tablespoons of sliced almonds can also be added for crunch factor.
Add pepper or Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning blend to flavor as desired.

title: Fresh Tofu Spring Rolls
description: These light and satisfying spring rolls provide protein from tofu, and together with the vegetables, add a fresh option to your kidney diet.
steps: Wash and dry the lettuce, then cut each leaf in half lengthwise. Cut carrots julienne style. Slice onion. Set aside.
Boil 6 cups of water and set aside to soak the rice wrappers later.
Drain and pat dry the tofu. Slice it into 12 pieces, each about 4″ long.
Spread the tofu on plate and season it evenly with cumin, granulated garlic, sea salt and black pepper.

Heat a non-stick pan with olive oil. Place the tofu strips in the pan, seasoned side down. Season the other side and fry until the bottom is lightly browned, about 1 to 2 minutes. Flip and fry until second side is lightly browned. Place the tofu on a plate to cool.

Pour hot water into a large shallow bowl. Dip a rice wrapper in hot water. Once it’s slightly soft, place the wrapper on a large plate and place 2 halves of the lettuce in the center of the wrapper. Sprinkle 2 to 3 tablespoons of carrot and 1­ to 2 tablespoons of sliced onion on top of the lettuce. Place one cooled tofu strip on top of the vegetables.
Fold the sides in, and then fold the bottom up and roll tightly. Repeat with the rest of the rice wrappers, vegetables and tofu strips.
Refrigerate and serve cold with your favorite low-sodium dressing.
hints: Serve with 2 tablespoons of low-sodium dressing. Miso ginger dressing is a good choice.

Although the amount of salt used in this recipe is minimal, some individuals may wish to further reduce sodium content by using salt-free seasoning. Mrs. Dash and Kirkland No Salt Seasoning are good alternatives.

title: Strawberries and Cream Oatmeal
description: Strawberries, oats and soy milk are the main ingredients in this high fiber one dish meal. Strawberries and Cream Oatmeal may become a breakfast favorite.
steps: Chop the strawberries, then coat with sugar or granular sweetener. Set aside.
Combine the water, soy milk and half & half in a small pot. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat.
Add the strawberries and bring to a boil.
Add the oats and cook 4 to 5 minutes to desired thickness.
hints: For extra sweetness drizzle with honey, agave or sweetener of choice.
Try raspberries or blueberries instead of strawberries when in season.
A single serving is considered as a one dish meal. If serving as a side dish, decrease portion to 1/2 cup
For a gluten-free diet check oatmeal for "gluten-free" on the label.

title: Campfire Trout
description: DaVita dietitian Helen not only knows her way around the kitchen, but she can also tell you how to get around Colorado. Helen shares some delicious kidney-friendly recipes, like Campfire Trout, and lays out a fun itinerary for visiting the Rocky Mountain state. Even if you can’t get to Colorado anytime soon, her recommendations will make you feel like you’ve taken a vacation.
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® Garlic & Herb seasoning blend
steps: Prepare charcoal coals.
Slice lemon and green onions. Chop celery and julienne carrots.
Place fish in the center of a large piece of foil (heavy-duty foil works best for a campfire). Sprinkle with Mrs. Dash seasoning.
Arrange lemon slices over fillets. Sprinkle with green onions, carrots and celery.
Seal foil tightly. Place on rack over campfire coals for 10 to 15 minutes or until fish flakes easily with a fork. (Be careful opening packet as steam will escape.)
hints: Bake fish in the oven at 400° F for 10 to 15 minutes if charcoal grill is unavailable.
If you are on a lower protein diet decrease portion to 2 ounces (cooked), 6 portions for the recipe.

title: Crunchy Tofu Stir Fry
description: Crunchy Tofu Stir Fry is a kidney-friendly vegetarian option. DaVita dietitian Jean from Iowa created Crunchy Tofu Stir Fry to share with kidney patients looking for meatless options that still provide high quality protein to meet the requirements of a dialysis diet.
serving_size: 1 cup tofu and vegetables + 1/2 cup rice
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning blend
steps: Cut tofu into cubes. Cut bell pepper into strips and chop garlic clove.
Mix reduced-sodium soy sauce, lime juice and sugar in a small bowl. Set aside.
In three separate bowls, put cornstarch, egg whites and bread crumbs. Dip tofu cubes first in cornstarch, then egg whites and coat with bread crumbs.
Heat canola oil in a skillet or wok and stir fry coated tofu until golden brown and crunchy. Remove tofu from pan and set aside.

In the same pan, add sesame oil. and heat. Stir fry broccoli and red bell pepper strips until crisp tender. Add chopped garlic, Mrs. Dash seasoning blend, black pepper and cayenne pepper and cook one minute.
Add tofu back to pan and toss with vegetables. Pour soy-lime juice mixture over top, sprinkle with sesame seeds and stir. Remove from heat and divide into 4 portions.Serve with 1/2 cup rice.
hints: Substitute olive oil for sesame oil if desired.
You can freeze cubed tofu to thaw and stir fry later. Freezing gives tofu a firmer, "meatier" texture.

Use your favorite salt-free seasoning. Tip: Penzey’s Spices®, Mrs. Dash® and Tone’s® make a variety of excellent salt-free seasonings. Avoid salt substitutes that contain potassium chloride due to high potassium content.

title: Hot Mulled Punch
description: Apples are versatile foods that score high when it comes to helping you stay healthy. Nothing beats that fresh apple flavor. In the chill of autumn, what could be more comforting than a nice cup of kidney-friendly Hot Mulled Punch, a yummy blend of cranberry and apple juices with a hint of cinnamon and cloves? This is a drink that smells as good as it tastes.
ingredients: 6 cups Ocean Spray® Natural Pure100% Unsweetened cranberry juice
steps: Combine ingredients in a large pot or crock pot.
Heat to a simmer and serve hot.
hints: Hot Mulled Punch can be simmered in a crock pot until ready to serve. It’s a great way to fill the house with fall fragrance.
For a lower carbohydrate version, diabetics can substitute low-calorie cranberry juice cocktail and Splenda® brown sugar blend. Carbohydrate = 24 grams per serving, 1-1/2 carbohydrate choices.

title: Frost on the Pumpkin Pie
description: Frost on the Pumpkin Pie Recipe submitted by DaVita renal dietitian Diane from Nebraska is an irresistable kidney-friendly Halloween dessert. Take it to your next party.
ingredients: 16 ounces Pillsbury® Creamy Supreme® Vanilla Frosting
steps: Heat oven to 350º F.
In small bowl, combine graham cracker crumbs, sugar, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, nutmeg, 1/4 teaspoon cloves and melted butter; stir until blended. Reserve 4 tablespoons of crumbs for topping.
Press remaining crumbs over bottom and up sides of two 9-inch pie pans.
Bake for 6 minutes. Cool.
In a large bowl, combine frosting, sour cream, pumpkin, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, ginger and 1/4 teaspoon cloves. Pour filling into prepared crusts.
Place mixing bowl and hand-mixer beaters in the freezer for 15 minutes. Put heavy cream in the bowl and beat until soft peaks form. Divide and spread evenly on top of each pie.
Sprinkle reserved graham cracker crumbs over top.
Freeze to set up, then refrigerate until ready to serve.
Store remaining dessert in refrigerator.
hints: You can buy graham cracker crumbs or make your own by crushing 36 graham cracker squares.

To reduce the fat use Reddi-Wip® dairy whipped topping instead of heavy cream and skip step #6. Instead of spreading on pie, spray about 2 tablespoons on each serving right before it is served. Fat is reduced to 3 grams.

title: Homemade Phosphorus-Free Baking Powder
description: There are many foods that are restricted for those with kidney disease and on dialysis, but thanks to DaVita renal dietitian Mary from Kansas, her recipe for Homemade Phosphorus-Free Baking Powder has put foods such as biscuits, tortillas, pancakes and waffles back on your menu.
serving_size: approximately 1 tablespoon per recipe (varies depending on number of servings and other ingredients)
steps: Sift together cream of tartar and baking soda using a fine strainer.
Store in an airtight jar or baggie at room temperature until ready to use.
hints: Note the amount and nutrients are used throughout a recipe, so the nutrient values will be spread out. Most recipes call for less than a tablespoon of baking powder for an entire recipe.

This baking powder recipe uses a 2-to-1 ratio of cream of tartar to baking soda. To replace one tablespoon of commercial baking powder in a recipe, use 2 teaspoons cream of tartar and 1 teaspoon baking soda.
You can use this mixture in the same proportion as commercial baking powder when making cakes, quick breads, muffins, tortillas, pancakes and waffles.

Cream of tartar is the potassium acid salt of tartaric acid, which is a by-product of wine making. One teaspoon contains 495 mg potassium. When using cream of tartar with baking soda to replace phosphorus-containing baking powder, be aware the potassium content of food will be higher but phosphorus is much lower.

title: Apple Bars
description: A healthy kidney-friendly dessert that’s tasty needs to be passed along. And that’s exactly what Sandra from Minnesota is doing with her delicious, low potassium and good-for-you Apple Bars.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350° F.
Peel and chop the apples.
Cream together 1/2 cup of the butter and the granulated sugar or granulated sugar substitute.
Add the sour cream, vanilla, baking soda, salt and flour. Stir to mix; add the chopped apples.
Pour the batter into a greased 9” x 13” baking pan.
In a small bowl, crumble 2 tablespoons of softened butter, the brown sugar and cinnamon together. Sprinkle over top of the batter.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes. Let cool completely.
To make icing, combine 2 tablespoons melted butter, milk (or milk substitute) and powdered sugar. Drizzle over top and cut dessert into 18 bars.
hints: 1 medium apple yields 1 cup chopped apples.

People with diabetes can replace the granulated sugar with a granular sugar substitute and omit the icing which will lower the carbohydrate content to 19 grams per serving (1 carbohydrate choice). Use caution with portion sizes.

title: Crab-Stuffed Celery Logs
description: Fancy enough for a party appetizer yet easy enough for a quick snack. That sums it up for Crab-Stuffed Celery Logs from the DaVita dietitian team. Try this kidney-friendly appetizer at your next event.
steps: Trim the celery rib ends. Drain and flake the crab meat. Mince the onion.
In a small bowl combine the crab meat, onion, mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Fill each celery rib with 1 tablespoon of the crab mixture.
Cut each celery rib into 3 pieces.
Sprinkle crab-stuffed celery pieces with paprika before serving.
hints: Recipe analysis includes canned crab meat. Substitute fresh or frozen if preferred.
Double or triple the recipe to serve at parties or social events.

title: French Fries Made with Eggplant
description: DaVita dietitian Jill’s Crispy Eggplant French Fries are an exciting kidney-friendly alternative to potatoes and are an excellent source of fiber.
ingredients: 3 teaspoons dry Hidden Valley Original Ranch® Salad Dressing and Seasoning Mix
steps: Peel and slice eggplant into 3/4” sticks, 4” long. Rinse and pat dry.
In a medium bowl, mix milk and eggs until well blended; stir in hot sauce.
In a wide, shallow bowl, combine cornstarch, bread crumbs, and dry Ranch salad dressing mix.
Heat oil in frying pan on high heat.
Dip eggplant sticks into egg mixture and then roll each piece in bread crumb mixture.
Place in oil, flipping regularly and fry 3 minutes or until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately.
hints: Substitute 1/2-cup low-cholesterol egg product to lower fat and cholesterol content.
French fried potatoes are much higher in potassium compared to French Fries Made with Zucchini.

title: Tempeh Pita Sandwiches
description: The next time you have a craving for a sandwich with crunch and a nutty flavor, try Tempeh Pita Sandwiches, a vegetarian favorite. In addition to fitting into a kidney-friendly diet, Tempeh Pita Sandwiches are low in cholesterol and saturated fat and high in fiber at 5.5 grams a serving.
steps: Cut tempeh into 12 slices. Thinly slice onion, bell pepper and mushrooms.

In a large skillet heat 1 tablespoon of the sesame oil over medium heat. Add sliced tempeh and cook each side for 3 to 4 minutes until browned. Add balsamic vinegar and cook one minute; flip and cook an additional minute. Remove tempeh from skillet.
Add remaining sesame oil to skillet and heat over medium heat. Add the onion, bell pepper and mushrooms and cook until tender.
Cut pita in half and open to form a pocket. Spread each half with 1 teaspoon mayonnaise. Add 3 pieces tempeh and 1/4 the vegetable mixture to each pita half. Serve immediately.
hints: For a flavor change replace sesame oil with your favorite flavored oil.
Tempeh made from whole soybeans mixed with rice or millet., then fermented. It has a nutty-flavor and absorbs flavors from marinades or seasonings added during cooking.

title: Pineapple Rice
description: Add a sweet, tropical taste to your next kidney-friendly side dish. Pineapple Rice is easy to make and makes a great impression.
ingredients: 1 cup canned pineapple tidbits in unsweetened juice
3/4 cup long grain white rice, uncooked
steps: Drain pineapple and reserve juice.
Mix together the pineapple, rice, reserved pineapple juice & water in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, cover and reduce heat. Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until all of the water is absorbed and the rice is tender.
hints: Serve with any of the curry recipes.

title: Asparagus Spread
description: Here is a kidney diet recipe for Asparagus Spread that makes tasty finger sandwiches and is a hit as a dip at parties. Kidney-friendly asparagus can be substitued with cucumbers in this recipe for a different taste sensation.
steps: Set cream cheese out to soften.
Drain asparagus well.
Combine all ingredients in a food processor and process until blended. Remove to a bowl, cover and refrigerate overnight.
Serve spread with low-sodium crackers or make finger sandwiches.
hints: Canned asparagus may be replaced with fresh or frozen asparagus. Boil in water until asparagus is soft enough to mash with a fork.
This recipe may be made with diced cucumber instead of asparagus.

title: Chile Colorado Sauce (Basic Red Chili Sauce)
description: Here’s a kidney-friendly recipe for Chile Colorado Sauce, which is simply Basic Red Chili Sauce. This is what gives your chili recipes its delicious, distinctive flavor.
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried red chile powder (ancho or pasilla)
steps: Finely chop onion and mince garlic.
In a medium saucepan heat canola oil and sauté onions and garlic until tender.
Stir in the flour until blended; add the cumin and oregano. Cook and stir for 3 minutes then remove from heat.
Add chili powder and stir to blend. Return pan to heat and add 2-1/2 cups water, salt and sugar.
Heat sauce to a boil, stirring constantly. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes.
Refrigerate sauce until ready to use. Makes 2-1/2 cups.
hints: Chili powder burns easily so stir frequently and be careful not to let your pan get too hot.
Make chili powder from dried chilies or use store bought chili powder. Be aware, chili powder has added salt so sodium content will be higher. Omit the 1/4 teaspoon of salt if chili powder is used.
Sauce keeps for 1 week in the refrigerator.
Use this sauce to make the Chile Colorado recipe.

title: Hot Holiday Cider (low sugar)
description: Many dialysis patients are on a fluid restriction, so when it comes to choosing a beverage they want to make it enjoyable. This kidney-friendly recipe for Hot Holiday Cider warms your taste buds and provides a delectable aroma to fill your home with the holiday spirit. Treat yourself, your family and your guests to a flavorful sip of Hot Holiday Cider this winter season.
steps: Pour cider into a Crock-Pot® and add cinnamon, cloves and allspice.
Heat and let steep for one hour to blend the flavors.
hints: This tasty beverage also brings a wonderful holiday fragrance to your house.

title: Southern Cole Slaw
description: This kidney-friendly cole slaw recipe gives a nice crunch to any BBQ sandwich or as a side at a picnic. The horseradish and pickle gives it a unique twist.
steps: Mince the green onions and pickle spear.
In a food processor, shred on high speed the carrots, cabbage and red cabbage and set aside.
In a separate large bowl, mix green onions, pickle spear and remaining ingredients.
Add the cabbages and carrots to the ingredients and mix until all colors are blended.
Chill in refrigerator for one hour.
hints: This is good on its own, on BBQ, and on tortilla chips as a snack.

title: Creamy Orzo and Vegetables
description: Michele from North Carolina is a natural in the kitchen, so when her husband Charlie required a kidney diet she went to work creating recipes for him. Creamy Orzo Pasta is just one of the tasty recipes made special for dialysis patients.
steps: Finely chop garlic. Chop onion and zucchini. Shred carrots.
In a large skillet heat olive oil over medium heat. Sauté the garlic, onion, zucchini and carrots for 5 minutes.
Add curry powder, chicken broth and salt; bring to a boil.
Add orzo pasta and stir until mixture returns to a boil. Cover and reduce heat to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally for about 10 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and pasta is al dente.
Add cheese, chopped parsley and the frozen peas. Heat until the vegetables are hot, adding a bit more broth if necessary to maintain creaminess. Add pepper to taste.
hints: Great served with chicken instead of potatoes or rice.
Recipe can be easily halved.
Small amounts of cheese, like the Parmesan cheese in this recipe, can be included and still maintain phosphorus and sodium in an acceptable range.
Chicken stock or broth contributes to the protein content of this recipe. Be sure to keep it low-sodium without added potassium chloride.

title: No-Bake Peanutty Oat Bars
description: Boost your fiber and protein intake with No-Bake Peanut Butter Oat Bars. Great for a quick breakfast, snack or dessert, these bars may replace your favorite pre-made kidney-friendly protein bar.
steps: Line a 5 x 7-inch or 8-inch square baking dish with wax or parchment paper.
In a medium bowl mix together oats, cinnamon and salt.
In a medium bowl mix protein powder, peanut butter and agave nectar; stir until smooth.
Mix the oats with peanut butter mixture until well blended.
Pat mixture evenly into lined baking pan. Sprinkle chocolate chips on top and pat down evenly. Refrigerate for at least one hour.
Cut into 5 sections then in half for 10 bars. If desired, wrap each bar in plastic wrap. Keep refrigerated until ready to eat or carry on the go.
hints: Honey may be substituted for agave syrup.
Substitute dried cranberries or cherries for chocolate chips.
Vanilla or unflavored protein powder can be used.

title: Hot Wassail
description: Hot Wassail is a great way to get folks to gather around. The delicious aroma of apple and cranberry juices along with an array of spices will warm your heart and put you in the holiday spirit.
steps: Mix all ingredients in a large Crock-Pot® and place on low heat until warm.
Serve and enjoy.
hints: Make this cider before holiday guests arrive to fill your home with a delicious aroma.

title: Chicken Teriyaki Pita Sandwich
description: There’s nothing more satisfying than a tasty meal that’s healthy. Jessica, a DaVita renal dietitian from California, shares her delicious and kidney-friendly recipe for Chicken Teriyaki Pita Sandwich recipe that fits the bill.
ingredients: 7 teaspoons Kikkoman® Less Sodium Teriyaki Sauce
8 ounces boneless, skinless chicken breast, uncooked
steps: Place chicken into a zip-top bag. Add 5 teaspoons teriyaki sauce and marinate in refrigerator for 3 to 4 hours.
Dice onion; chop scallions, lettuce and tomato.
In medium frying pan heat 1 tablespoon oil and cook chicken thoroughly until no pink remains.
Meanwhile, in a small frying pan, sauté onion in 1 tablespoon olive oil.
While chicken and onion are cooking, combine mayonnaise, scallions and 2 teaspoons Kikkoman® Less Sodium Teriyaki Sauce. Put mixture aside.
Cut each cooked chicken breast into several strips.
Take pita halves and coat inside with mayonnaise mixture. Fill pita with several chicken pieces; top with sautéed onion, lettuce and tomatoes.
hints: One average-size raw, boneless, skinless chicken breast weighs approximately 4 ounces. Flatten breasts for more even cooking.
If smaller pitas are substituted for the larger ones, use one pita per serving
Even though tomato is a high-potassium vegetable, the 2 tablespoons per serving is small enough that potassium for the recipe is still acceptable for a low-potassium diet.
If you need extra calories, use regular mayonnaise instead of reduced fat. Besides providing more calories, sodium content is lower.

title: Easy Pantry Pasta
description: Rely on your pantry to create kidney-friendly meals from items you already have on hand. That’s what DaVita dietitian Elyse did to create this Easy Pantry Pasta recipe that’s low in sodium and high in flavor.
ingredients: 5 ounces low-sodium tuna packed in water, canned or pouches
1 cup canned cannellini beans (rinsed and drained)
1/2 cup no salt added tomato sauce
1/2 cup no salt added canned green peas
steps: Cook pasta according to directions for al dente doneness, omitting salt. Drain while reserving 1/2 cup cooking liquid. Slice the roasted red peppers.
In a large pan over medium heat, combine remaining ingredients except peas and parmesan cheese.
Add drained pasta to sauce mixture and stir to combine. Add some of the reserved cooking liquid if sauce appears too thick.
Add green peas and parmesan cheese; stir.
Serve with a whole grain roll. Enjoy!
hints: Look for the canned or bottled roasted red peppers with the lowest sodium content. Fresh roasted red peppers can be substituted.
Penne pasta works well but you can use whatever is in your pantry. Whole grain and whole wheat pasta also work well with this recipe.
If using gluten-free pasta, rinse pasta after draining to avoid a gummy result and do not reserve pasta cooking liquid. Instead add 1/2 cup low-sodium broth if sauce appears too thick.
Reduce serving size or the amount of pasta in the recipe if a lower carbohydrate meal is needed.
Add extra tuna if more protein is needed.

title: Home-Style Vanilla Ice Cream
description: Here’s a frosty, creamy vanilla ice cream treat that’s low in phosphorus. DaVita renal dietitian Kelly from Louisiana created this special version of Home-Style Vanilla Ice Cream especially for her dialysis patients and she’s pleased to share it with you.
ingredients: rock salt and ice (for ice cream machine)
steps: Using a 1-quart, microwavable bowl, beat egg product and sugar until well blended.
Stir in non-dairy creamer and microwave for 1 minute, or until mixture thickens.
Remove from heat. When cool, stir in vanilla.
Pour mixture into center container of the ice cream machine.
Layer ice and rock salt around container, alternating layers until bucket is full.
Process according to manufacturer’s instructions for your particular ice cream machine.
hints: If you have an ice cream machine, pour mixture in and follow manufacturer instructions.
This recipe may be doubled. Freeze extra for a later treat.
Variations can be made by adding 1-1/2 cups of low-potassium fruit of choice such as fresh strawberries or peaches. When adding fruit, increase sugar to 2/3 cup.

Coffee Rich® non-dairy creamer and Egg Beaters® low-cholesterol egg product were used in the development of this recipe. If these brand-name products are not available in your area, ask your renal dietitian about substitute products.
One serving counts as 4 ounces of liquid in a dialysis diet.

title: Nondiary Ice Crème Sandwiches
description: Not everyone can tolerate ice cream, but thanks to DaVita administrative assistant Mechelle from South Carolina, they can enjoy Nondairy Ice Crème Sandwiches. Her kidney-friendly recipe is a cinch to make.
steps: Break graham crackers into squares (2-1/2″).
Spread 2 tablespoons Reddi-Wip® topping on 10 of the graham cracker halves.
Top with the remaining 10 graham cracker halves to make sandwiches.
Place sandwiches on a cookie sheet and freeze for 2 hours before serving.
hints: This recipe can be made in batches and kept frozen for a yummy snack later.
Wrap each sandwich in plastic wrap and place in a freezer bag.
Check graham crackers for phosphate additives before purchasing.

title: Summer Squash with Pineapple and Peppers
description: When summer squash is plentiful but you’re short on time, DaVita dietitian Christie has the perfect kidney-friendly recipe. Summer Squash with Pineapple and Peppers is prepared in a slow cooker so you can fill the pot and leave it until dinner time.
steps: Cut squash into 1-inch cubes. Dice bell pepper into small pieces.
Placed cubed squash in a slow cooker.
In a small bowl, mix the green bell pepper, pineapple with juice, cinnamon, brown sugar and melted butter.
Spoon over squash and mix well.
Cover squash and cook on low heat setting for 6-7 hours or until squash is tender.
Stir gently to mix before serving.
hints: People with diabetes may use Splenda® Brown Sugar Blend. Reduce the portion to 2-1/2 tablespoons to reduce carbohydrate to 8 grams per serving.
Cook on high heat setting for 4 to 5 hours if quicker cooking time desired.

title: Lime Caribbean Dressing
description: DaVita dietitian Judy has created yet another tasty, easy to prepare salad dressing that’s lower in fat and sodium compared to commercially prepared dressings. Lime Caribbean Dressing is tasty, has only 4 ingredients and is versatile. Add it to salad or coleslaw, or use it as a dip for chicken fingers or grilled shrimp.
steps: Zest one of the limes and set aside.
Juice both limes into a small bowl.
Add mayonnaise and pineapple preserves to lime juice and whisk together until well blended.
Fold in lime zest. Stir in a few drops of hot sauce if desired.
hints: Serve Lime Caribbean Dressing over iceberg lettuce or blend with shredded cabbage for a Caribbean twist on traditional coleslaw.
Try as a dip for grilled chicken fingers or shrimp on the Bar-B!

title: Hearty Squash Casserole
description: DaVita renal dietitian Jennie from Georgia knew she wanted a career in healthcare, but nursing wasn’t for her. She always enjoyed cooking so when she discovered dietetics, Jennie knew she found her calling. Now you can sample one of Jennie’s personal recipe creations, Hearty Squash Casserole. This vegetarian squash casserole makes a great side dish to liven up your vegetable selection.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Process whole wheat bread in food processor until crumbled.
Slice squash and then microwave with water for 16 minutes or until tender.
Drain squash well in colander.
Grate fresh carrots and chop sweet onion.
Combine squash, carrots, sweet onion, salt, 1 tablespoon flaxseed and eggs. Blend well.
Add 1/2 of the whole wheat bread crumbs. Mix in.
Spray 9″ square pan with nonstick cooking spray. Pour mixture into baking pan. Set aside.
Melt butter and then add remaining bread crumbs and remaining flaxseed to make topping. Mix well.
Spread topping over casserole.
Bake for 30 minutes or until topping starts to brown.
Cool and cut into 8 servings.
hints: Feel free to substitute zucchini for yellow squash.
Use Vidalia® or other sweet onion.
Flaxseed is a good source of dietary fiber and omega-3 fatty acids.

title: Quick Fruit Sorbet
description: DaVita dietitian Helen not only knows her way around the kitchen, but she can also tell you how to get around Colorado. Helen shares some delicious kidney-friendly recipes, including Quick Fruit Sorbet, and lays out a fun itinerary for visiting the Rocky Mountain state. Even if you can’t get to Colorado anytime soon, her recommendations will make you feel like you’ve taken a vacation.
ingredients: 20 ounces canned crushed pineapple, juice-packed, frozen
steps: Thaw pineapple just enough to get out of can.
Place all fruit in food processor and process until pureed.
Serve immediately or spread into an 8” x 8” pan and freeze.
hints: You can freeze unopened can of pineapple.

title: Easy Pumpkin Cheesecake
description: Pumpkin Cheese Cake from the Davita renal dietitian team is a way to incorporate pumpkin flavor without adding too much potassium.
steps: Preheat over to 375º F. Brush pie crust with egg white and bake for 5 minutes. Reduce oven heat to 350º F.
Combine softened cream cheese, sugar and vanilla in a large bowl. Beat with mixer at high speed until smooth.
Beat in egg substitute. Add pumpkin puree and pumpkin pie spice and blend until smooth.
Pour pumpkin mixture into pie shell and bake 40 to 50 minutes until center is set. Cool pie, then refrigerate.
Cut into 8 slices. Serve each slice with 1 tablespoon desssert topping.
hints: Pumpkin is high in potassium but the amount of potassium for one piece of cheesecake is only 126 mg since only 1/2 cup pumpkin is used in the recipe.

title: Deviled Eggs for Parties
description: Deviled Eggs for Parties is the perfect kidney-friendly appetizer to make for your next get-together. This recipe is good for people with kidney disease, diabetes or those on dialysis.
steps: Boil eggs for 15 to 20 minutes.
Let eggs cool for approximately 1 hour.
Slice eggs in half, lengthwise and scoop out the yolks.
Combine the yolks, mayonnaise, mustard and pepper; mix well.
Stuff yolk mixture into egg white halves and sprinkle with paprika.
hints: Use low-fat mayonnaise if you are watching your fat intake.

title: Multigrain Hot Cereal
description: Tired of bland and mushy hot cereals on the renal diet? Try this tastier alternative. Multigrain Hot Cereal is a cooked cereal mixture of whole and refined grains with an appealing flavor and texture.
steps: Boil water in a 1-1/2 quart covered pot.
Add grits; stir briefly.
Add bulgur, buckwheat, and oats; stir briefly.
Reduce heat to a vigorous simmer; liberally spray nonstick cooking spray on simmering surface.
Cover pot; simmer for 25 minutes.
Remove pot from burner; stir in couscous.
Let pot stand covered for 8 minutes, then serve.
hints: If desired, drizzle with honey or your favorite sweetener. Add unsalted margarine or butter, blueberries or dried cranberries before serving.
Makes a thick cereal. Thin by adding water or milk substitute in 1/2 ounce increments.
Refrigerate extra serving and reheat in the microwave for 30-60 seconds for a quick breakfast.
You can buy smaller amounts of grains if you shop at a market that offers grains in bulk containers. Find a variety of grain products at supermarkets, natural food stores and on the internet.

title: Braised Short Ribs of Beef
description: Enjoy the kidney-friendly recipe Braised Short Ribs of Beef at your next dinner.
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Chop carrot, celery and onion.
Trim fat from ribs. Combine 1/2 cup flour and pepper. Roll short ribs in flour to coat.
Heat 1-1/2 tablespoons oil in a skillet, and brown ribs on all sides.
Place ribs in a roasting pan and roast uncovered for 45 minutes. Carefully pour off extra fat.
Heat 1/2 tablespoon oil in a large pot and sauté chopped vegetables until soft.
Add roasted short ribs and beef broth. Cover and simmer 2 hours or until ribs are tender.
To make gravy, brown 2 tablespoons flour in 1 tablespoon oil. Add 1 cup of the meat liquid and stir over medium heat until thickened. Serve 2 tablespoons of gravy with each serving of short ribs.
hints: Look for reduced sodium broth containing 500 milligrams sodium or less per 1 cup serving. Avoid low sodium broths and bouillons containing potassium chloride—it’s very high in potassium.
Braised means to cook covered in a small amount of liquid, usually after browning the meat to help develop color and flavor.

For CKD non-dialysis: This higher protein recipe may be appropriate for your diet if the portion size is adjusted to reduce protein content. Adjustments should be based on your individual protein prescription. Check with your dietitian if you are unsure.

title: Seafood Dip
description: Seafood Dip is such a great choice for those on the kidney diet. Lorraine, a DaVita dietitian from Massachusetts, created a renal-friendly dip by substituting healthy alternatives. Low in saturated fat, shrimp combined with imitation crab made from fish provides high quality protein. The no salt added ketchup in the cocktail sauce contains lycopenes, an antioxidant from tomatoes that helps keep your heart healthy.
ingredients: 1 cup Hunt’s® no salt added ketchup
steps: Remove cream cheese from the refrigerator to soften. Do not soften in the microwave.
Thaw shrimp per package directions. Remove the shells and any visible veins on the shrimp and cut into small pieces.
Chop the imitation crabmeat into small pieces.
Stir the shrimp and crabmeat together and place in the refrigerator.
In a small bowl combine ketchup, horseradish, lemon juice and Worcestershire sauce to make a low-sodium cocktail sauce.
In a medium bowl, stir the softened cream cheese until it becomes creamy.
Slowly add cocktail sauce to the cream cheese. Stir thoroughly.
Add a small amount of Tabasco® sauce to the cream cheese. Stir thoroughly. Sample the cream cheese mix. Add more Tabasco® sauce as needed.
Add shrimp and crabmeat to the cream cheese. Stir thoroughly. Sample the cream cheese mix. Add more Tabasco® sauce as needed.
Cover and chill in refrigerator overnight.
Serve with low-sodium crackers.
hints: Expecting a crowd? Make a large batch by doubling the ingredients.
This recipe can be made the same day, but does taste best if prepared the night before.
Low-salt Ritz® crackers pair excellently with the dip.
Low-fat cream cheese may be substituted but sodium and phosphorus is higher.
Definitely do not use fat-free cream cheese, as this will compromise the taste.
Some low-sodium ketchup brands contain potassium chloride instead of salt. Avoid these brands because the potassium is much higher.

title: Cinnamon Smoothie
description: Boost protein intake while keeping phosphorus low with this easy to make Cinnamon Smoothie.
steps: Combine cinnamon and sugar.
Add 2 ounces egg whites. Mix well.
Add vanilla and stir.
Add balance of egg whites and stir.
Add whipped topping and mix until dissolved.
hints: Low-cholesterol egg whites is pasteurized. It is safe to consume without cooking. Do not use raw egg whites.
People with diabetes can substitute sugar-free sugar substitute if desired. Carbohydrate is reduced to 6 grams per serving if sugar substitute is used instead of sugar.

title: Rice Idli
description: Rice Idli is a dish popularized in India. Enjoy this kidney-friendly version created by the mother of a DaVita patient.
ingredients: 1 cup black lentils, uncooked, split without skin
steps: Soak rice and lentils in water. Grind the lentils in a food processor or liquidizer to a smooth paste.
Grind rice not too fine, a little coarse. Mix the two pastes and add salt. Let the batter ferment for 12-14 hours at a warm place (avoid the inside of the oven or on top of a gas stove).
Just before cooking, add the baking soda. Steam idlis on idli moulds. Serve with sambar.
hints: Lentils contribute extra potassium and phosphorus, so portion must be limited to 2 rice idles.
Sambar is a vegetable stew containing pigeon peas, tamarind, vegetables and ground spices. It is very popular in southern India.
Serve with cilantro chutney or with a dollop of butter topped with a spoon of sugar.

title: Chajita Chicken Sandwich
description: If you’re wondering what to do with leftover chicken, try turning it into something special with DaVita dietitian Heidi’s Chajita Chicken Sandwich recipe. It’s high in fiber and flavor and a perfect fit for a kidney diet.
steps: Slice chicken breasts into strips. Dice onion and bell pepper.

In a skillet, sauté chicken, onions, bell pepper and seasonings (cumin, garlic and onion powders) in coconut oil for 8 to 15 minutes or until chicken is cooked thoroughly. Stir occasionally. If mixture in skillet becomes too dry, add water. Turn off heat when chicken is fully cooked.
Turn on Panini maker or George Foreman Grill. Or set a dry skillet on medium heat.
Combine salsa and sour cream. Spread 2 teaspoons salsa mixture on a slice of bread for each sandwich.
Spoon 1/4 of chicken mixture on top of bread with salsa mixture.
Sprinkle 1 teaspoon cheddar cheese on top of chicken mixture for each sandwich. Put the second piece of bread on top.

Put sandwich in Panini maker or George Foreman Grill for 3 to 5 minutes or until bread is slightly toasted. If using a skillet, toast for 3 to 5 minutes or until bread is slightly toasted on one side, and then flip the sandwich and press down with a spatula to cook the second side for 3 to 5 minutes or until bread is slightly toasted.
hints: Use any color of bell peppers for variety.
Select the lowest sodium products for salsa and other prepared foods. Compare labels between brands as there may be a big difference.

title: Feta Pasta with Chicken and Asparagus
description: DaVita dietitian Jill presents a zesty and kidney-friendly taste of Italy and Greece that’s excellent for lunch or dinner, Feta Pasta with Chicken and Asparagus.
steps: Trim asparagus and cut on diagonal into 1” pieces. Cut chicken into cubes.
Bring a large pot of water to boil. Add pasta, and cook as instructed on box or about 8 to 10 minutes. Do not add salt. Drain, and set aside.

Warm 3 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Stir in chicken, and season with pepper and garlic powder. Cook until chicken is cooked through and browned, about 5 minutes. Remove chicken to paper towels.
Pour chicken broth into the skillet. Add asparagus, chopped garlic, a pinch more of garlic powder, oregano and pepper.
Cover and steam until the asparagus is just tender, about 5 minutes.
Return chicken to the skillet, and warm through.
Stir chicken mixture into pasta and mix well. Let sit about 5 minutes.
Drizzle with remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil, stir again, and then sprinkle with feta cheese.
hints: One-pound fresh asparagus yields approximately 2 cups when trimmed.
Feta cheese is very high in sodium. This dish was made low sodium by limiting feta to 1/4 cup, omitting salt and using low-sodium broth.
2 average chicken breasts without bones or skin is approximately 8 ounces.

title: Pineapple Salsa
description: Most people hear "salsa" and automatically think tomato salsa, but really, salsa is a spicy sauce that can be created with any fresh vegetable or fruit that will make a tasty condiment. For people on hemodialysis, high potassium tomatoes are out and low potassium pineapples are in with this recipe for Pineapple Salsa.
steps: Mince onion, garlic and jalapeno. Chop cilantro.
Drain pineapple and place in non-reactive bowl. Add other ingredients and mix well.
Refrigerate several hours or overnight to blend flavors.
hints: Serve Pineapple Salsa on tacos or fish or chicken entrees.

title: Easy Phosphorus-Free Drop Biscuits
description: There are many foods that are restricted for those with kidney disease and on dialysis, but thanks to DaVita renal dietitian Mary from Kansas, her recipe for Homemade Phosphorus-Free Baking Powder has put foods such as her Easy Phosphorus-Free Drop Biscuits back on your menu.
ingredients: 1/2 cup chilled unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
steps: Preheat oven to 450° F.
In a large bowl, combine flour, phosphorus-free baking powder, sugar and salt.
With a pastry blender or fork, cut the buuter into flour mixture until it resembles course crumbs.
Add nondairy creamer, 1/4 cup at a time, and mix lightly until moistened.
Drop batter by the tablespoon onto a lightly greased baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden on the edges, about 8 to12 minutes.
Serve warm.
hints: Cream of tartar is the potassium acid salt of tartaric acid, which is a by-product of wine making. One teaspoon contains 495 mg potassium. When using cream of tartar with baking soda to replace phosphorus containing baking powder, be aware the potassium content of food will be higher but phosphorus is much lower.
Limit to one biscuit if you are on a low-potassium diet.

title: Kiwi-Berry Fruit Salsa
description: Make this kiwi berry fruit salsa for your party. DaVita’s recipes are delicious, kidney-friendly, and submitted by DaVita dietitians.
steps: Wash the outside of the kiwis and remove the skin. Dice.
Wash apples, strawberries and raspberries. Core the apples, then dice. Cut the tops off the strawberries; dice the strawberries and raspberries.
Place all the fruit in a bowl, and add brown sugar and preserves. Stir gently until well mixed.
Chill salsa in the refrigerator overnight.
hints: Serve with low-sodium crackers or tortilla chips. Look for brands with the lowest amounts of sodium

You may also serve with homemade pita chips. Split the pitas in half and cut each half into quarters. Spray with cooking spray and bake at 350º F for about 8 minutes. If desired, sprinkle a mixture of cinnamon and sugar after you spray the pita with cooking spray.
Drain salsa in a fine sieve to remove extra fluid if you are on a fluid restriction.

title: Stuffed Zucchini Boats
description: DaVita dietitian Tammy from North Carolina takes the guesswork out of yummy veggies with her Stuffed Zucchini Boats. Savory and kidney-friendly, this dish works well as a snack or paired with an entire meal.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon original Mrs. Dash ® seasoning blend
steps: Pre-heat oven to 375° F.
Cut zucchini in half lengthwise. Using a spoon, scoop out seeds, forming a trench in each zucchini half.
Place zucchini in a pot of boiling water, and boil for 3 to 5 minutes.
While zucchini is cooking, toast 2 slices of bread.
Place toast and 2 uncooked pieces of bread in food processor to make bread crumbs.
Add seasonings to bread crumbs and mix well.
Add 1/2 cup of the zucchini cooking water and blend with a fork to get the consistency of stuffing.
Remove zucchini from water and place in 8 x 8” baking dish, peel side down.
Spoon stuffing into trench in each zucchini half.
Bake for 20 minutes and serve.
hints: Substitute one large zucchini and serve 1/4 instead of 1/2 medium squash pieces.

title: Chicken Lo Mein
description: Who doesn’t love Chinese food with its signature crunchy veggies and lively sauces?! Lo mein means “stirred noodles” in Cantonese, and the dish is sautéed or flash-wokked differently from Chow Mein, which is stir-fried. The kidney-friendly recipe was modified by Laura from Texas, and the great thing about it is that leftover chicken (or beef) from a cookout works perfectly as the meat-base—nobody will know you’re using leftovers!
steps: Cook lo mein noodles according to package omitting salt. Drain and set aside.
Thinly slice chicken breasts.
Heat olive oil in a wok or big, deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and sauté for 4 to 5 minutes or until no longer pink.
Add onions, carrots and celery. Stir-fry gently until vegetables are cooked but still crunchy, about 4 to 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms and noodles, and stir constantly until hot.
Add soy sauce, stir and serve.
hints: Linguine or fettuccine can be used instead of lo mein noodles. The nutrient composition is very similar.
Replace chicken with thin slices of beef for variety.
Use leftover grilled chicken or beef from a cookout the day before. In step #3, reduce cooking time to 1 to 2 minutes.

title: Crock-Pot® Chicken
description: Crock-Pot® Chicken is a super-simple recipe that fills the need for easy, budget-friendly and kidney-friendly meals with an ability to s-t-r-e-t-c-h. Salt-free, this dish is suitable for dialysis and diabetes food plans.
ingredients: 2 teaspoons Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning blend
steps: Wash chicken and remove the inside giblets if they are included.
In a small bowl combine seasoning blend, pepper and garlic powder.
Sprinkle half the seasonings inside the chicken. Rub the remaining seasoning on the outside of the chicken.
Place the chicken breast-side-up in an oval crock-pot or neck-up in a round crock-pot.
Cover and cook on low setting for 8 hours.
Remove chicken from bones and discard the skin.
hints: No liquid or fat needs to be added. Chicken will make its own liquid/broth.
Use the chicken in recipes that call for cooked chicken, or to make chicken salad or chicken soup.
Make chicken broth with the bones and skin.
To make chicken soup, add egg noodles, low sodium broth, carrot shreds and celery to diced chicken and broth.
If you are on a lower protein diet, adjust the portion to match your meal plan.

title: Chinese Hotdish (Casserole)
description: DaVita renal dietitians from Minnesota share some of their favorite regional recipes that have been modified for the dialysis diet. By limiting phosphorus,potassium and sodium,dialysis patients can enjoy delicious Chinese Hotdish. Hotdish is another name for casserole,and those seem pretty popular in Minnesota.
ingredients: 1 can (10.5-ounces) Healthy Request Condensed Chicken Noodle Soup
1 can (10.5-ounces) Healthy Request Condensed Cream of Chicken Soup
3/4 cup Uncle Ben’s® white converted rice, dry
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Dice celery and onion.
In a large skillet, brown ground beef, celery and onion. Drain.
Pour cooked ground beef into a 2-quart casserole baking dish.
Using a wooden spoon, mix in chicken noodle soup, cream of chicken soup, Worcestershire sauce, rice and boiling water and mix thoroughly.
Cover and bake for 50 minutes.
Remove dish from oven and stir.
Sprinkle chow mein noodles over top of casserole.
Bake an additional 10 minutes, uncovered.
Let stand 15 minutes before serving.
hints: Compare chow mein noodle nutrition labels and select the brand lowest in sodium

title: Mr. P’s Curried Turkey with Rice
description: Compliment this kidney-friendly recipe for Mr. P’s Curried Turkey with Rice with a cucumber side salad.
steps: Heat a 2-quart heavy saucepan over medium heat.
Add butter and melt, then add garam masala (or spice substitute*)
Cook for 1 or 2 minutes until spices become fragrant.
Add the diced onion and sauté until soft and golden.
Cut turkey breast into 1″ cubes. Add the turkey, raisins and apple to the pan and sauté for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the rice and stir.
Add the chicken stock, bring to boil and cover.
Cook on medium-low heat until rice has absorbed all of the liquid, about 20 minutes.
Add the peas during the last few minutes to heat through, then toss and serve.
hints: Compliment this dish with a cucumber salad (sliced cucumbers, thin sliced onion, white vinegar, black pepper and sugar or sweetener).
Spice substitute for garam masala: Combine 1/2 teaspoon cardamom, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg, 1/4 teaspoon coriander and 1/4 teaspoon cloves.
If you have diabetes you may need to reduce the rice portion if carbohydrate content is too high.

title: Veggie Strata
description: Roselyn, a DaVita dietitian from Colorado, brings her 37 years of experience and her love for food to her dialysis patients and you. Always striving to find delicious and exciting vegetable options, she offers a scrumptious kidney-friendly Veggie Strata.
steps: Cut bread into cubes. Place on a baking sheet and bake at 225° F for 15 minutes. Turn cubes over and continue baking 15 minutes or until dry and crisp.
Dice onion, mushrooms and bell pepper.
Melt butter in a small skillet and sauté onion, mushrooms and red peppers.

Grease a 9” square baking dish with nonstick cooking spray. Arrange half of the bread cubes in a single layer in the dish and sprinkle with half of the vegetable mixture. Arrange spinach leaves on top.
Form a second layer with remaining bread and vegetables on top.
Whisk together eggs, vinegar, half & half creamer, Worcestershire sauce, hot sauce and black pepper. Pour evenly over the bread.
