Cover surface with plastic wrap and refrigerate at least 1 hour or overnight.
Allow strata to stand at room temperature for 20 minutes.
Pre-heat oven to 325° F. Remove plastic wrap and bake 50 minutes.
Remove from oven and sprinkle cheddar cheese over the top. Cook for an additional 10 minutes or until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean.
Cut into 9 servings and serve hot.
hints: Look for a rustic-style artisan white bread or a sourdough round loaf. Slice 1/2 inch thick. Compare breads and select the lower sodium choice.
Look for half and half without "phos" in the ingredient list, this would indicate a phosphate additive, which should be avoided.

title: Cranberry Orange Biscotti
description: DaVita renal dietitian, Meg from Alabama, knows how to make a crunchy snack treat that is kidney-friendly and easily fits into a diabetic diet. Try her remarkable recipe for Cranberry Orange Biscotti.
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Place parchment paper on a baking sheet.
In a medium bowl sift together flour and baking powder.
In a large bowl beat sugar, butter, orange zest and salt with a mixer. Add eggs, one at a time and mix until well blended. Slowly add flour mixture and mix until all flour is incorporated.
With a spoon, mix macadamia nuts and cranberries into dough.
Remove dough from bowl onto a very lightly floured surface; form dough into a loaf that is approx 12” long and 3” wide.
Place on a baking sheet and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until barely golden on surface. Remove from oven cool loaf for 30 to 40 minutes.

Cut the cooled loaf into 3/4”-thick slices using a bread knife. Place slices back on the baking sheet and bake for another 15 minutes until biscotti are lightly golden. Remove from oven and cool on a rack.
hints: Cooking times vary with each oven.
Biscotti can be stored in an airtight container for about one week.
Great for gift-giving around the holidays.

title: Ginger Fruit Smoothie
description: This smoothie has a kick of ginger and a a bit of protein from Greek yogurt. Try it for a snack or breakfast.
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth.
Divide into 2 glasses.
hints: Frozen fruit is a great option if fresh isn’t available. If using frozen, you can omit the ice.
Protein powder is a great way to add protein to your diet but if you are trying to stick to a low protein diet, the recipe is delicious without.

title: Steamed Semolina Idlis
description: Serve Steamed Semolina Idlis for breakfast or dinner. The kidney-friendly recipe was created by the mother of a DaVita patient.
steps: Chop chili pepper, cabbage, and carrots. Mince ginger root.
Heat oil in a pan and add the mustard seeds. When seeds splutter add semolina and brown until it becomes light gold. Remove from heat and cool.
Mix yogurt, water, salt, baking soda, green chili and ginger into a smooth batter.
Grease idli molds lightly with a small amount of ghee.
Sprinkle some of the cabbage, carrot and peas into each mold. Top with the batter and steam for 15 minutes.
Serve hot. Make 12 idlis.
hints: Use batter immediately for best results.
Curious about unfamiliar ingredients? Semolina is the starch component of wheat kernels. It is known as farina or Cream of Wheat in the US. Ghee is clarified butter.

title: Hearty Faux Pho
description: This warm soup can be an quick and easy meal for any season.
ingredients: 1/4 cup low sodium egg or rice noodles
1/4 cup frozen peppers and onion blend
steps: Carefully add 8 ounces of very hot water to a wide mouth 16 ounce mason jar.
Season the water by adding the first three ingredients: coconut amino, crushed ginger and apple cider vinegar.

Next layer in the noodles, cooked shredded chicken and frozen vegetables. Tighten lid and let stand ten minutes or until noodles are tender. If jar has cooled, remove the lid and microwave to preference for warmth, 30 seconds at a time. Add additional toppings of cilantro, green onion and lime, if desired.
hints: This recipe is designed to limit fluid to 8oz. It may help to invert the mason jar a few times during the process in order to cover all the ingredients.
If using additional toppings, this adds a small amount of potassium, approximately 22 mg of potassium.

title: Old Fashioned Short Bread Cookies
description: Who knew three simple ingredients — margarine, brown sugar and cake flour — could create such a tasty treat? Try this kidney-friendly recipe for Old Fashioned Short Bread Cookies and see for yourself.
steps: Cream margarine and beat in sugar until soft and fluffy.
Add flour and mix. Knead dough to incorporate the flour. Form into a ball.
Wrap dough in plastic wrap and chill for at least 1 hour.
Roll dough out about 1/4” thick on a lightly floured board.
Cut with cookie cutters, or with a knife into diamond shapes. Bake cookies on a lightly greased cookie sheet at 325° F for 10 minutes or until lightly browned.
hints: Decorate cookies with cinnamon, colored sugar or icing for a holiday touch.

title: Tuna Ceviche
description: Maria, a DaVita dietitian from Arizona, believes a healthy diet can make the difference in improving quality of life. Her primary goal with patients is developing a diet that provides the proper balance of potassium and phosphorus, which is crucial to maintain physical wellness. Maria’s exciting Tuna Ceviche recipe is zesty, healthy and kidney-friendly.
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning blend
18 saltine crackers, unsalted tops or 12 low-sodium whole wheat crackers
steps: Drain tuna and pour into a small mixing bowl. Flake with a fork.
Chop cilantro and onion.
Mix the cilantro, onion, black pepper and Mrs. Dash seasoning and blend with the tuna.
Pour fresh lemon juice over the tuna mixture and mix ingredients well.
Cover and place in refrigerator to marinate for at least 2 hours.
Serve 1/4 cup ceviche with 6 saltine crackers, unsalted tops or 4 low-sodium whole wheat crackers.
hints: If low-sodium, canned tuna is unavailable, look for the brand of tuna lowest in sodium and rinse under running water for 1 to 2 minutes to further reduce sodium content.
Traditional ceviche is made from raw fish or seafood marinated in lemon or lime juice. Acid from the lemon “cooks” the fish. This is a safer version of ceviche for kidney patients.
Substitute parsley for cilantro if desired.
Water crackers and low sodium triskets are great replacements for the unsalted saltines or whole wheat crackers.
